items.title: Bob Rosengarden interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 6, 1996
items.q: Skitch Henderson for example, who was a conductor, at that time a piano player with Frank Sinatra.

ctx.x: We’ve heard it a number of times.

And I also learned an important lesson, there are only two kinds of music: good music and bad music. So I tried to play as much good music as I possibly could. And worked © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -3-

my way up, you know, after the war, worked in night clubs, The Copa and Bill Millers of the era, owned by that mythical organization. And met some people who were very helpful and still are. Skitch Henderson for example, who was a conductor, at that time a piano player with Frank Sinatra. And I found myself a job at NBC because Skitch’s lady friend, Faye Emerson, who was a wonderful movie star and a funny, bright woman, a beautiful woman, and she was a friend of Mr. Sarnoff which was very helpful.
